title: Company-wide policies & processes (access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. It is intended for all employees, hiring managers, approvers, and operational owners.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors with system or data access.
- Covers cloud and on-prem resources, internal tools (Slack, Okta, GitHub, Datadog), finance systems, and vendor interactions.

Ownership and governance:
- Policy owner: People Ops (owner_team field).
- Operational owners: Security (access controls), Eng Infra (change windows), Finance (procurement/expenses), Legal (contracts), IT Ops (travel & booking integrations).
- Review cadence: Annual review or earlier when regulatory or business changes require updates.

1) Access & Permissions
Principles:
- Least privilege by default.
- Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) for services when supported.
- Time-bound elevated access for emergency or ad-hoc work.

Onboarding / Offboarding:
1. New hire access: hiring manager completes the Access Request template (see Internal Templates).
2. Provisioning: People Ops triggers identity lifecycle in Okta and creates tickets in the Identity queue (Jira/ServiceDesk).
3. First 30 days: mandatory access review with manager to confirm privileges.
4. Offboarding: People Ops initiates deprovisioning date in Okta; all active sessions are revoked and device access is removed.

Access request flow (standard role request):
- Requester completes the Access Request form (link in Internal Templates).
- Request routes to: 1) Manager approval, 2) Service owner approval, 3) Security review if access to sensitive data.
- Expected SLA for standard requests: 3 business days.

Privileged access and break-glass:
- Privileged roles (DB admin, KMS admin, infra root) require Just-In-Time (JIT) access via the PAM tool and approval from two approvers (manager + team owner).
- Emergency (break-glass) process: call the on-call security engineer, complete a post-facto change ticket within 24 hours, and document reason/impact.

Periodic audits:
- Quarterly automated entitlement reports generated from Okta/GitHub/GCP IAM, reviewed by service owners.
- Any anomalous privileges must be remediated within 7 days or escalated to Security leadership.

CLI example (access request creation):
- ticket create --template access-request --user "alice@redwood.com" --roles "data-analyst" --expires "2026-06-01"

2) Change Management
Change types:
- Routine: low risk, pre-approved by owner (no global outage risk).
- Standard: pre-authorized changes with runbook and backout plan (e.g., config flips, minor infra upgrades).
- Major: requires CAB approval and maintenance window (e.g., database migration, model serving runtime upgrade).
- Emergency: immediate mitigation for incidents; must follow emergency change process and retrospective.

Approval matrix and flow:
1. Submit Change Request (YAML snippet example below) to Change Management queue.
2. Automated triage assigns change type and required approvers.
3. Approvals required: service owner, SRE lead (for infra), Security (if affects data), Product owner for customer-facing features.

Change request example (metadata YAML):
---
change_id: CM-2026-1234
summary: "Upgrade runtime kernel for model-serving-1"
change_type: "major"
owner: "eng-serving-runtime-team@redwood.com"
start_window: "2026-05-10T02:00:00Z"
end_window: "2026-05-10T05:00:00Z"
backout_plan: "roll back to kernel v1.4 and restart workers"
impact: "Possible 5-15% latency increase during rollout"
---

Change windows and scheduling:
- Default maintenance window: Tuesday and Thursday 02:00-06:00 UTC for non-critical services.
- Major changes: require 2-week notice and a coordinated rollback plan with SRE.

Emergency changes:
- Trigger: active incident or critical vulnerability.
- Process: notify on-call SRE and Security, implement mitigation, open an emergency change record within 4 hours, and follow with a post-mortem.

Testing and rollout controls:
- Canary rollout: minimum 5% traffic for 30 minutes with auto-roll back criteria (error rate > 1% or latency 2x baseline).
- SLOs to monitor during change: 99th percentile latency and error rate; thresholds documented per-service in Dashboards & Alerts.

3) Data Management
Data classification:
- Public: safe for public disclosure.
- Internal: company-internal, not customer-specific.
- Confidential: customer data, PII, or regulated data.
- Restricted: highest sensitivity - encryption at rest + strict access control (KMS + HSM).

Handling and storage:
- Confidential & Restricted data: stored only in approved environments with encryption (AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit), KMS key usage logged.
- Avoid storing customer PII in third-party SaaS without an executed DPA and approval from Legal.

Retention and deletion:
- Retention schedule (examples):
| Data category | Retention period | Owner |
|--------------|------------------|-------|
| Application logs (internal) | 90 days | Eng SRE |
| Audit logs (security) | 365 days | Security |
| Customer backups | 7 years or per contract | Product/Legal |

- Data deletion: owners must maintain deletion runbooks and confirm via automated jobs.

Backups and recovery:
- Daily incremental backups, weekly full backups, and monthly restore tests for production-critical data.
- RTO target for production DBs: 4 hours; RPO: 1 hour.

Data transfer and third-party access:
- All cross-border transfers must be approved by Legal and Security.
- Vendor access to data requires scoped access, audited sessions, and a signed data processing addendum.

Example S3 lifecycle policy (JSON described as text):
- Transition to infrequent access after 30 days, to Glacier after 365 days, delete after 1825 days (5 years).

4) Procurement & Expenses
Procurement request process:
1. Initiator completes the Procurement Request template with business justification, estimated cost, and supplier info.
2. Routing: Manager approval -> Finance (review budget) -> Legal (if contract required) -> Procurement ops (vendor setup).
3. Procurement SLA: standard requests processed within 10 business days; expedited requests (<= $5k) within 3 business days.

Approval matrix (examples):
- <= $1,000: Manager approval
- $1,001 - $25,000: Manager + Finance
- > $25,000: Manager + Finance + VP approval

Payment and invoicing:
- Preferred payment method: company card for <= $5k or invoice via AP for larger purchases.
- All vendor invoices must reference an approved purchase order (PO) ID.

Expenses and travel reimbursement:
- Employees must submit expenses within 30 days of travel/event using the Expense template (see Internal Templates).
- Receipts required for expenses >= $25. Per-diem rules apply for meals when no itemized receipts are available.
- Fraud or pattern abuse will be investigated by Finance; repeated violations lead to disciplinary action.

5) Vendor Management
Vendor onboarding checklist:
- Business case and approval from sponsor owner.
- Security & Privacy review: completed security questionnaire and risk assessment.
- Legal: executed contract and DPA if vendor handles customer data.
- Procurement: vendor added to vendor registry and payment terms set.

Vendor risk review cadence:
- High-risk vendors: quarterly security reviews and annual contract renewal checklist.
- Low-risk vendors: annual review.

Vendor access controls:
- All vendor accounts scoped to least privilege and time-bound.
- Multi-factor authentication (MFA) required for vendor admin access.

Offboarding vendors:
- Revoke credentials, remove integrations/webhooks, and confirm data return or secure deletion as per contract within 30 days of termination.

6) Travel Policies
Pre-approval and booking:
- All business travel requires manager pre-approval via Travel Request template.
- Employees should use the company-approved booking portal (Concur partner link in Internal Templates) where available.

Travel safety and emergency contacts:
- Employees traveling to high-risk regions must notify People Ops and receive travel safety briefing.
- Emergency contact: People Ops on-call + Security duty phone (listed on the Travel template).

Allowable expenses and per-diem:
- Economy class for flights < 6 hours; Premium Economy approval required for flights >= 6 hours with Manager+Director approval.
- Hotel booking: mid-tier business hotels; upgrades require pre-approval.
- Per-diem: $60/day domestic, $100/day international (unless actuals submitted with receipts).

Expense submission:
- Submit expenses within 30 days via Expense template with receipts attached.
- Card charges that are personal must be paid back to the company within 14 days or will be deducted per payroll policy.

7) Internal Templates and Examples
Available templates (links in the templates page):
- Access Request template (Access Request form)
- Change Request template (YAML/JSON metadata example)
- Procurement Request form
- Travel Request and Expense templates
- Vendor Security Questionnaire (standardized CSV/Doc)
- PRD template for product teams

Quick template examples included below (as text):
Procurement Request (fields): requester_email, cost_center, description, supplier_name, estimate_usd, manager_approval, legal_required (yes/no), requested_by_date

Access Request (fields): requester, user_email, role_requested, justification, expiry_date, manager_approval, service_owner_approval

Change request minimal checklist:
1. Description and impact statement
2. Owner and rollback plan
3. Monitoring and alert thresholds
4. Communication plan and customer notification if applicable
5. Post-change validation and retrospective date

Compliance, training, and exceptions
- Training: All employees must complete annual Security & Data Handling training; People Ops tracks completion.
- Exceptions: Any deviation from these policies requires a documented exception request routed to the policy owner and approved by the relevant stakeholder(s). Exception approvals are recorded and expire after 90 days unless renewed.

Appendices and references
- Related docs: RBAC standards, Change Management Guidelines, Secure SDLC, Vendor Registry.
- Contacts: People Ops (people-ops@redwood.com), Security (security@redwood.com), Finance (finance@redwood.com), Legal (legal@redwood.com).

Revision history:
- 2025-09-15: Initial draft by Aisha Patel.
- 2026-04-22: Updated procurement thresholds, added canary rollback criteria, clarified vendor offboarding timelines.
